source_refs.note: 'Accuracy and Error' under topic 6.7, as printed (PDF 85, printed 81).

blocks.text: Accuracy shows how many predictions are correct out of the total predictions. It is measured as a percentage. High accuracy means better performance. The error shows incorrect predictions. Error rate is the opposite of accuracy. Accuracy alone may be misleading sometimes. Balanced data gives better accuracy results. Error analysis helps find mistakes. Both measures are important for evaluation. The accuracy equation is:

items: TP (True Positives): Number of correctly predicted positive instances.
TN (True Negatives): Number of correctly predicted negative instances.
FP (False Positives): Number of incorrectly predicted positive instances.
FN (False Negatives): Number of incorrectly predicted negative instances.
